review.review: The hero remained alive at 40/40 HP when the planner stopped. Decision 1464 selected a doorway retreat toward door 782; its accepted move closed door 914 behind the hero and hid the enemies. The retreat selector then discarded its plan because fewer than two enemies were visible, while escape protection correctly rejected exploration back through the same door. Decisions 1465–1468 alternated recovery and exploration instead of continuing the observed retreat route. A healing potion was consumed before the same contradiction ended in planner exhaustion at decision 1472. A local source-pinned reconstruction matched the original selecting helper at decision 1464, then confirmed cancellation on the recorded next input; this is not a reconstruction of all original runtime memory. The focused correction preserves an accepted retreat through temporary occlusion using recent sightings only as movement constraints, with fresh visible-step checks and existing hazard, health, pressure and input budgets intact. The new regression fails on the original policy and passes on the candidate; the full suite passes 1,865 tests with four skipped. No alternative gameplay was dispatched, and neither reaching the destination nor survival is established.
review.learnings: Losing sight of pursuing enemies behind a closing door is not clearance evidence. Preserve an accepted retreat when its next observed step remains admissible, rather than letting exploration immediately reverse it. Continue to require fresh safety checks and real collection evidence.
